hero.tagline: Where twilight gathers the day's last glow

today.heading: The longest light — solstice approaching
today.intro: June ninth. The year tilts toward its brightest edge, and the evenings stretch like honey across the horizon. In this slow crescendo of light, the meadow holds its breath — tulips open, lilies lean toward the sun, and the air itself seems painted. Midsummer is not a day but a feeling: the world luminous, abundant, and briefly, impossibly still.

visualAsset.description: Impressionist meadow at midsummer peak — tulips and lilies swaying in golden light, brushstroke sky

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Borrowed brilliance in a silver sky
moon.intro: What does it mean to glow without burning? The Moon answers each night: receive completely, return everything, hold nothing back. This is not diminishment — it is the deepest form of generosity. A silver chariot crossing the dark, asking nothing of the sun it mirrors, the Moon demonstrates that reflection itself is a kind of faithfulness.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The wave forgets it is the sea
philosophy.intro: The ego is a wave insisting on its own outline. For one bright instant it crests, certain of its separateness — then dissolves back into the depth that never left it. This is not tragedy. The sea does not mourn the wave. To stop performing individuality is not to disappear but to arrive, finally, at the substance beneath the shape.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Freedom beyond the fruit of action
gita.intro: Between two armies, with arrows nocked and drums pounding, the deepest wisdom in human literature was spoken — not in stillness but in the heart of chaos. The Gita's radical invitation: do not withdraw from the world to find truth. Immerse yourself completely, act with full commitment, and release your grip on what the action yields. Freedom lives not in the outcome but in the quality of the doing.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: The drum that speaks the universe
shiva.intro: A single beat on the damaru and the universe begins — not as metaphor but as literal truth. Shiva's dance is every atom's movement, every star's orbit, every breath drawn and released. The Tandava does not distinguish between dancer and dance, between the drum's vibration and the silence that contains it. To witness this is to understand that stillness and motion are one gesture, seen from different distances.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Light as the only subject
art.intro: Beauty happens in the space between — between eye and horizon, between hand and canvas, between one breath and the next. A sunflower conspires with the dawn to turn light into living gold; a lily transforms still water into sky. The impressionist knew what the mystic knows: nothing is owned, nothing is fixed. Every act of seeing is an act of creation, and every creation is a collaboration with what already shines.
